payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_ledger.py::test_a_regate_is_one_fact_that_folds_back_as_the_tasks_newest_row stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'A `_drop_task_rows` that leaves `regates` alone, so `fold_task(key, [])` keeps the row.' applied to saffron/ledger.py as an edit. The claim was "`Ledger.record_regate(task_id, *, head_sha, baseline_sha, new_failures)` files one `task_regate` fact under the task, with those three values as its payload. It commits one `regates` row per task, and a later call for the same task replaces that row whole. An id that names no task raises `ValueError` and writes no row and no fact. `Ledger.regate(task_id)` returns the task's row as a `sqlite3.Row`, or `None` for a task with no row. It returns `None` on a fresh ledger before any write, too. A fold of the record into a fresh ledger rebuilds every row, and so does a fold into the ledger that wrote them. `fold_task` with no facts removes the row its key filed. A ledger file whose table was dropped gains it again on open. The witness drives two tasks. It writes the second one twice and then the first. Every write uses three values that differ from each other and from every other write's. Each read uses a fresh `Ledger` on the same path.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
